findings_qualitative.value: Random motions dominate below ~30 pc; ordered motions dominate in the largest structures, consistent with galactic rotation

evidence.quote: we find that most structures on $\lesssim30$ pc scales tend to have larger random motion than ordered motion.

evidence.quote: We find a similar power law slope as that reported for NGC 253

claims.hypothesis: Ordered vs random motion dominance depends on scale
claims.result: random dominant ≲30 pc, ordered at larger scales
claims.finding: Ordered motion driven by large-scale processes

evidence.quote: The former appears stronger in gas structures at $\gtrsim30$ pc while the latter becomes more dominant at $\lesssim30$ pc.

claims.hypothesis: Self-gravity vs motions at different scales
claims.experiment: Compare t_ff with t_cr of ordered and random motions
claims.result: t_ff comparable to t_cr,ord at all scales; longer than t_cr,rand below ~10 pc
claims.finding: Random motions can counter self-gravity at small scales, modulo alpha_CO uncertainty

evidence.quote: Modulo uncertainties with the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor, the estimated gravitational free-fall time is comparable to the crossing time of ordered motions for structures on all spatial scales
